submission.natural_language_explanation: Phrase-frame head: it attends (weight >0.8) to one earlier token that opens the current phrase or line and writes on the 1-6 tokens after it. Strongest (0.5-1.0 of max) on a superlative noun phrase's head noun and the qualifier that follows it ('the largest forest [in]', 'the best player [on]', 'greatest driver [ever]', 'worst pain I've [ever]', 'busiest [nights]'), with 'most'/'-est'/'best'/'worst' attended. Weaker (0.25-0.6) on: 'first/only/last ... to' and comparatives ('the more ... the better you get', 'faster than anyone else in'); attribution after a closing quote (', she said'); code declaration bodies after func/class/private/#define; and templated lines repeated two or more times (math Q&A drills, answers after 'What is ...?\n', '(1887-1951),' name entries). Ordinary narrative prose, a single short sentence-initial clause, plain comma or number lists, and repeated names without a line template stay below 0.25 of max.
